To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intention to attend a screening was the most important predictor of actual attendance, but that the strength of the intention was influenced by a number of health beliefs and by causal attributions.

the causal attribution of high blood pressure to stress and anxiety, the belief that high blood pressure is serious, the perceived susceptibility to high blood pressure, the belief that there is a cure for high blood pressure, and a high perceived benefit of the high blood pressure screening were all significant predictors of intention to attend.
patients who attribute HBP to factors that are controllable and who believe that HBP is serious, are more likely to attend screening.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between health beliefs and causal attribution in relation to a health behaviour, attendance at a screening for high blood pressure.
the synthesis of two models of health behaviour, the Health Belief model and Attribution theory.
the development of a model of health behaviour, which incorporates a variety of factors that are known to affect health-related behaviour.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HBM is not an adequate model of health-related behaviour.
causal attribution is a powerful predictor of behaviour.
causal attributions, as a psychological construct, are important in relation to both health beliefs and health behaviour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Health Belief and Attributional Models are not competing theories, but complementary approaches.
the combination of the two approaches is more useful than either one alone, in terms of the prediction of behaviour.
causal attributions, as well as health beliefs, have an impact on health-related behaviour.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HBM and Attribution Theory are complementary in explaining health-related behaviours.
we can predict which patients will attend a screening for high blood pressure by looking at their health beliefs and causal perceptions.
we need to be aware of the impact of the patient's perception of the disease on their behaviour.
